title: Collections and typed data structures — concept map
intro: Typed arrays, Map/Set generics, tuple types, readonly views, the satisfies operator, and typed array methods — how TypeScript models JavaScript collections at compile time while types erase at emit.

overviewDiagram.title: Collections learning path
overviewDiagram.source:
flowchart LR
  A["T[] vs tuples"] --> B["Map / Set / Weak"]
  B --> C["satisfies operator"]
  C --> D["readonly collections"]
  D --> E["typed map/filter/reduce"]
  E --> F["TS vs C# collections"]

conceptCards.title: Arrays vs tuples
conceptCards.summary: T[] is homogeneous variable length. [T1, T2] fixes arity and per-index types — useState, HTTP pairs.

conceptCards.title: Map and Set generics
conceptCards.summary: Map<K,V> accepts any key type. Set<T> deduplicates. WeakMap for GC-friendly object metadata.

conceptCards.title: satisfies operator
conceptCards.summary: Validates shape without widening literal keys — config tables and never exhaustiveness.
conceptCards.example: const ROUTES = { home: '/' } satisfies Record<string, string>;

conceptCards.title: readonly collections
conceptCards.summary: readonly T[] blocks mutation at compile time — shallow only. Covariant in element type.

conceptCards.title: Typed array methods
conceptCards.summary: filter needs type predicate to narrow. reduce needs explicit accumulator generic.

conceptCards.title: C# collection mapping
conceptCards.summary: TS generics erase — JSON boundaries need validation. List→T[], Dictionary→Map/Record.
conceptCards.example: validate unknown into User[] after fetch
